rule: Offer multiple alternative calls-to-action (phone, message, form) instead of a single lead-capture button.

finding: Test #437 (2,595,541 visitors): +1% MDE lift in leads when alternative CTA ('Send Message') added alongside primary phone CTA

rule: Surface alternative entry points (e.g., gift purchase option) earlier in the funnel rather than deep in checkout flow.
quote: an additional purchase trigger was added - the ability to start by chosing a gift announcement option. In the control, this same question was asked further in the purchase funnel (after adding to cart).
finding: Test #446 (100,016 visitors): +6.5% sales lift when gift announcement option moved from post-cart to initial purchase trigger

rule: Position product recommendations and highlights at the top of the page, not the bottom, to increase cart additions.

rule: Show popular products higher on homepages and category pages to drive sales increases.
quote: three popular juice products were shown higher on the variation (instead of lower in the control). Impact on sales was measured.

rule: Expand clickable areas to the full size of interactive elements, not just portions, to improve progression and conversions.
quote: the click area of job listing tiles was expanded to the size of the full job tile

rule: Extend button width to match form width above it to improve lead generation and signups.

rule: Show completed steps with distinct visual states in progress bars to aid step recognition.

rule: Test progress bar visibility against breadcrumbs; circular bars show overall steps but reduce clickable step visibility.

rule: Adding a cheaper plan option increases cart additions and conversions in subscription contexts.

quote: the cheapest pricing plan was removed from a set of 2 options. This only left the most expensive pricing plan as the option.

rule: Add pricing information to landing page headlines to signal cost expectations early and increase signup intent.
quote: the headline was changed to reflect pricing information (informing that trades are starting at $3). Impact on progression and signups was measured.

rule: Display pricing beside action buttons to set cost expectations before users commit to an application or purchase.

rule: Display free shipping messaging prominently near price information to increase add-to-cart and sales conversion.

finding: Meta-analysis of 6 tests shows combined positive effect on sales (p-val reported); individual tests on product pages with 96,962 and 97,277 visitors each showed measurable sales lift.

rule: Show a congratulatory message on the add-to-cart button confirming free shipping and returns to reinforce the purchase decision.
quote: the button label changed to a cheering message which congratulated the user on his choice and ensuring that shipping is free.
finding: Test on Snocks.com with 56,067 visitors measured completed transactions as primary metric.

rule: Add popular product categories as clickable links on the homepage to increase search initiation and sales conversion.
quote: popular search terms were added at the bottom of a long e-commerce homepage. Hence, the variation showed additional search triggers that lead to results pages.
finding: Test on Mvideo.ru with 5,469,900 visitors showed 46.3% median effect on sales; test with 2,278,698 visitors achieved 80% statistical power at 1.7% minimum detectable effect.

rule: Display brand logos with links to product listing pages on the homepage as an additional navigation layer to improve discoverability.

finding: Test on Online.metro-cc.ru with 1,716,300 visitors measured completed sales; achieved 17.8% statistical power at 1% minimum detectable effect.

rule: Use reduced padding between form fields on search forms to minimize overall visual weight and suggest lower effort for task completion.

rule: Test highest-impact hypotheses in isolation; avoid bundling changes that could mask negative effects with positive ones.
quote: test your highest probability ideas first

rule: Combine only changes with proven positive probability; test unknowns separately to avoid canceling out gains.
quote: only group the positive probability changes into your big leap variation, while pushing all unknowns into separate variations
